brief.headline: Aluminium broke its losing run and tightened its curve on the same ring, and the weekly close this page had pre-registered as the decisive technical test landed six dollars on the right side of it - the first session in this window where every internal leg pointed the same way.
bullets: WHAT MOVED: on Friday's LME official aluminium cash settled $3,254.00 and three-month $3,267.00. Cash rose $26.00, or 0.81%, the first rise after falling on six of the previous seven settled sessions and the largest single-session gain of the sequence. Three-month rose $14.50, or 0.45%. The market is shut on Saturday, so this is the last trading session's official and the correct figure to carry; it was verified complete rather than lagging on the English and German overviews and on all five per-metal daily tables, with five-for-five stock-line reconciliation.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN THE PRICE: the cash-to-three-month contango NARROWED $11.50 to $13.00 from $24.50, which was the widest reading of this sequence. That is the first narrowing in five rings and it removes almost half the contango in one session. Because cash rose nearly twice as fast as three-month, the curve tightened while the flat price rose - spread and price pointing the same way for the first time in five rings. Cash below three-month is contango; the published reversal condition, a backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official, is still unmet.

THE TECHNICAL TEST RESOLVED, AND IT RESOLVED CONSTRUCTIVELY: Friday's official is the weekly close, and this page had published in advance that a weekly close beneath 3,261 would shift weight materially towards a bearish alternate count. Three-month settled $3,267.00, six dollars above it. The test is closed in favour of the constructive count. Six dollars is a thin margin and is stated as thin rather than dressed up.

WHAT TO WATCH, AND WHERE THE PRESSURE STILL IS: visible LME stock was unchanged at 241,375 tonnes for a second session, so the front tightened on an inventory that did not move - whatever tightened it is not visible in warehouse data. Against the constructive read, public customs data published Friday show China's August primary aluminium imports down 14.65% year on year at 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 96% of them, while Chinese aluminium extrusion exports hit a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes with a September pullback guided - both point to a weakening ex-China pull. The US ten-year Treasury yield pushed on to 5.214%, a further multi-year high. Next official: Monday 28-September, 13:20 London.

drivers.text: Chinese primary imports fell 14.65% year on year in August, which means less Chinese competition for ex-China metal — Public customs data reported on 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports at 185,500 tonnes, DOWN 14.65% year on year and up just 0.16% month on month, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total and Australia (2,920 t), Indonesia (2,180 t) and Malaysia (1,800 t) accounting for almost all of the remainder. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. THE STATED CAUSE IS STRUCTURAL RATHER THAN DEMAND-LED: domestic capacity is at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling, end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient, and inventory is being drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports. WHY IT MATTERS FOR PREMIUMS EVEN SO: a premium is set by competition for units at a location. China importing 14.65% less primary metal, and 96% of what it does import arriving from a single discounted-origin supplier, means the marginal ex-China unit faces less Chinese competition - which works against premiums in Japan, Europe and the United States regardless of why Chinese buying fell.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China Aug aluminium imports down 14.7% year on year, Russia accounts for 96% of supply (25-September-2026)

drivers.text: Chinese semis exports hit a 2026 high, which pressures converter margins in exactly the markets where premiums are assessed — Public data reported on 25-September show China's August aluminium extrusion exports at 92,500 tonnes, the highest monthly figure of 2026, up 9.7% year on year from 84,300 tonnes and 3.0% month on month from 89,800 tonnes, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. SEPTEMBER IS GUIDED LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking; the share of processing trade rose while ordinary trade fell, which the source reads as marginal weakening in price-driven independent orders. THE PREMIUM READ IS SPECIFIC: extrusions compete with locally converted metal in third markets. More Chinese semis arriving in South-East Asia, Africa and Latin America pressures the converter margins that ultimately support regional ingot premiums, even though the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately rather than netted.
drivers.source: AL Circle - China's August aluminium extrusion exports hit a YTD high; pullback expected in September amid narrowing price spread (25-September-2026)

logistics.note: REVIEWED WEDNESDAY 23-SEPTEMBER-2026. THE MOST CONSEQUENTIAL NEW PUBLIC INFORMATION THIS RUN IS DIPLOMATIC RATHER THAN OPERATIONAL, AND IT CUTS BOTH WAYS. SMM's 23-September summary records that on 22-September US President Trump, speaking at the 81st UN General Assembly, reiterated that the United States would reach an agreement with Iran AFTER THE NOVEMBER MIDTERM ELECTIONS; that Iranian Foreign Minister Araghchi met US envoy Witkoff in New York and Trump described a three-hour meeting with the Iranian delegation as very productive with another to be arranged; and that Iran has publicly set CONDITIONS for reopening the Strait of Hormuz - immediate lifting of the maritime blockade, immediate unfreezing of all Iranian assets, and an end to the war on all regional fronts. READ THIS CAREFULLY RATHER THAN OPTIMISTICALLY. A negotiation is now visibly under way, which is the first genuine de-escalation signal of this cycle. But the publicly stated US timetable puts any agreement AFTER November, and Iran's stated conditions are maximalist. The transit constraint is therefore still in force today and is not publicly guided to clear inside this quarter. TREAT THESE AS REPORTED DIPLOMATIC STATEMENTS, NOT AS SETTLED OUTCOMES. WHY THE ARROW IS CUT FROM UP TO FLAT AND NOT TO DOWN: the direction of news has genuinely changed - talks are happening, are described by one party as productive, and a reopening condition set has been publicly articulated, which is more than existed at any point in this cycle. But NOTHING OPERATIONAL HAS CHANGED. The prior evidence stands unrefuted: Reuters tracking cited 20-September put daily commodity transits at 3-6 ships between 2 and 18 September against a normal ten-day average of 12-18, and a tanker was reportedly struck near Khasab, Oman on 18-September with the attribution still UNCONFIRMED. The second-order freight evidence also stands: SMM's 17-September bauxite weekly records Guinea-to-China ocean freight at around $39-42/wmt, a lane that never touches the Strait, because regional disruption withdraws tonnage from the global pool and reprices capacity everywhere. headlines.title: THE CONTANGO NARROWED $11.50 TO $13.00 FROM THE WIDEST READING OF THE SEQUENCE, AND IT IS THE FIRST NARROWING IN FIVE RINGS. Cash settled $3,254.00 against three-month $3,267.00 on the 25-September official, against $24.50 the session before. Almost half the contango was removed in a single ring. Cash below three-month is contango. Because cash rose $26.00 while three-month rose $14.50, the flat price and the curve moved in the SAME direction - both towards tightness - for the first time in five rings. The published reversal condition, a backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official, is still UNMET, so this is an improvement rather than a regime change.

THE LOSING RUN BROKE ON THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION GAIN OF THE SEQUENCE. Cash rose $26.00, or 0.81%, to $3,254.00 after falling on six of the previous seven settled sessions. Three-month rose $14.50, or 0.45%, to $3,267.00. THE HONEST CONTEXT: cash is still $30.84 BELOW the September-to-date official cash mean of $3,284.84 and only $4.37 above the August mean of $3,249.63. One session recovers part of a month, not the month.

THE PRE-REGISTERED WEEKLY CLOSE TEST AT 3,261 RESOLVED IN FAVOUR OF THE CONSTRUCTIVE COUNT, BY SIX DOLLARS. Friday's official sets the weekly close, and this page published in advance that a weekly close beneath 3,261 - the 38.2% retracement of the 3,855-to-3,061.5 decline - was the condition for shifting weight materially to the bearish weekly alternate. Three-month closed $3,267.00. The alternate is NOT promoted, the daily-degree alternate raised on 24-September is left where it is, and the six-dollar margin is published as thin rather than dressed up as decisive.

VISIBLE STOCK WAS UNCHANGED AT 241,375 TONNES FOR A SECOND CONSECUTIVE SESSION, SO THE FRONT TIGHTENED WITHOUT ANY VISIBLE INVENTORY SIGNAL BEHIND IT. That is the one leg of today's board that did not confirm, and it is the reason this page will not call a regime change off one ring: whatever bid for immediacy did not show up in warehouse data. What survives is the level and the week - a 1,225-tonne or 0.50% draw from 242,600 on 18-September, a level near multi-decade lows and about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215.

CHINA'S AUGUST PRIMARY ALUMINIUM IMPORTS FELL 14.65% YEAR ON YEAR TO 185,500 TONNES, AND RUSSIA SUPPLIED 96% OF THEM. Russia accounted for 178,150 tonnes, with Australia 2,920, Indonesia 2,180 and Malaysia 1,800 making up almost all the rest. Net imports were 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67% year on year but up 6.44% month on month. January-August imports were 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. The cited cause is structural - domestic capacity at the 45-million-tonne policy ceiling with inventory drawn down through semis exports rather than primary imports - and end-use demand from grid investment, electric vehicles and photovoltaic mounting is described as resilient. THE BALANCE EFFECT IS THE SAME WHATEVER THE CAUSE: less Chinese pull on ex-China units, which is the load-bearing assumption of the ex-China tightness case.

CHINESE ALUMINIUM EXTRUSION EXPORTS HIT A 2026 HIGH OF 92,500 TONNES IN AUGUST, UP 9.7% YEAR ON YEAR AND 3.0% MONTH ON MONTH, taking January-August to 629,600 tonnes, up 8.7%. South-East Asia took 26,500 tonnes or 28.6% and was the only region with both the largest volume and double-digit growth; Africa took 18,800 tonnes and Latin America 14,400. September is guided LOWER at 85,000-92,000 tonnes because the China-to-overseas price spread has narrowed, compressing margins on independent order-taking, with processing trade gaining share and ordinary trade losing it. More Chinese semis in third markets pressures the converter margins that support regional ingot premiums, even while the same exports support Chinese domestic ingot demand. The two effects are opposite and are stated separately.

CHINESE PRE-HOLIDAY DESTOCKING REMAINS THE STRONGEST FUNDAMENTAL NUMBER AVAILABLE AND IS CARRIED AT ITS OWN DATE. SMM's statistics for 24-September record aluminium ingot inventory at major domestic consumption sites down 63,000 tonnes on 17-September and a further 55,000 tonnes on 24-September - 118,000 tonnes across two weeks, described as the steepest fall for that period in the 2020-2026 record. SMM publishes this series on Mondays and Thursdays, so no new print is due before Monday 28-September and nothing here has been rolled forward. THE BUILT-IN LIMIT, RESTATED: the named drivers are pre-holiday stockpiling and a widening spot-futures spread, and both reverse by design after the 01-08 October holiday.

THE LAST PUBLIC CHINESE SPOT REVIEW STILL SHOWS METAL CLEARING AT DISCOUNTS, AND IT IS CARRIED AT 24-SEPTEMBER RATHER THAN RE-STAMPED. SMM's South China review for 24-September records transactions concentrated at a premium of 250-290 yuan/tonne over the SHFE 2610 contract but quotes lowered repeatedly through the session, with most deals concluded at actual discounts, phased stockpiling complete, procurement slowing and spot circulation shifting to oversupply. The stated dominant driver was the need to cash out before the holiday. This is the clearest live tension on the page: the exchange is paying more for immediacy while the largest physical market is clearing at discounts.

CAST ALUMINIUM ALLOY INGOT INVENTORY ENDED A SIX-WEEK BUILD, FALLING 2,700 TONNES WEEK ON WEEK TO 31,800 TONNES on SMM's 24-September print. The attributed causes are a widening spot-futures spread and the release of pre-holiday stockpiling demand, with improved purchasing appetite. Further destocking is anticipated into the holiday, but the source itself flags that whether demand is sustained AFTER the holiday warrants attention. Carried at its publication date; no newer print is due before Monday.

THE ALUMINA PANEL DID NOT PRINT AND IS CARRIED AT 24-SEPTEMBER. SMM's weekly alumina index is 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, essentially flat, with regional prices stable. The ratio that matters DID move, and only because the metal did: alumina at $363.60/t against the 25-September three-month of $3,267.00 is 11.13%, down from 11.18%, against a decade norm of 15-17%. That is a smelter-margin improvement delivered entirely by the revenue line. Next scheduled index print: Thursday 01-October.

CHINESE ALUMINA SUPPLY IS AMPLE AND THAT IS SUPPORTIVE FOR SMELTER MARGIN, CARRIED AT 24-SEPTEMBER. SMM reports China's national weekly alumina operating rate at 76.89% on 119.62 Mt/y of capacity, so roughly a quarter of installed refining capacity is idle and available to respond to any sustained price signal. A seaborne alumina market that is firm because of shipping frictions, sitting on top of a refining industry running at three-quarters of capacity, is not a structural alumina shortage - and that is the reason this page does not treat firm FOB Australia prints as a threat to smelter margin.

THE US TEN-YEAR TREASURY YIELD PUSHED ON TO 5.214%, ADDING ABOUT SEVEN BASIS POINTS TO YESTERDAY'S 5.142% AND EXTENDING A MULTI-YEAR HIGH. Higher long rates raise the cost of carrying inventory, push forward curves towards contango, and raise the discount rate on every metals project and equity. IT IS THE MOST PERSISTENT BEARISH INPUT ON THIS PAGE AND TODAY IT DELIVERED THE CLEANEST EVIDENCE AGAINST ITS OWN EXPLANATORY POWER: on the identical session the aluminium contango NARROWED $11.50. If financing cost were the dominant driver of the aluminium curve, that should not have happened.

EUROPEAN GAS FELL 4.02% TO EUR 71.93/MWh, THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION FALL OF THIS WINDOW, AND BRENT SLIPPED 0.56% TO $106.01. Lower European gas cuts the marginal cost floor, which is bearish for price, while directly improving the economics of the European smelting capacity publicly guided to return - Slovalco's first 75,000 tonnes of 175,000 is guided for Q4-2026. It also supports European converter margins. The effects run in opposite directions and are stated separately rather than netted into a single verdict.

THE DOLLAR EASED AND TWO CONSECUTIVE SESSIONS OF DOLLAR STRENGTH ENDED. The dollar index fell 0.32% to 100.966 and the LME euro fixing rose 0.30% to 1.14030 from 1.13690, with the European Central Bank fixing at the same 1.14030 and the public reference rate at 1.14037 - all three agree, so there is no divergence to flag in the currency leg. A softer dollar mechanically makes dollar-priced metal cheaper for non-dollar buyers and is a mild support for the flat price, consistent with the direction of the aluminium price on the same session.

THE CROSS-METAL FRONT SIGNAL CHANGED SIGN FOR A FOURTH CONSECUTIVE SESSION, WHICH VINDICATES YESTERDAY'S DECISION TO RETIRE IT AS A REGIME READ. On the 25-September ring aluminium's contango narrowed to $13.00 from $24.50 and zinc's backwardation widened to $108.00 from $65.50 - two fronts towards immediacy - while copper's backwardation narrowed to $93.00 from $125.00, nickel's contango widened to $180.00 from $155.00 and lead's widened to $26.50 from $25.00. WHAT IS DURABLE AND CUTS THE OTHER WAY FROM YESTERDAY: aluminium had loosened its front on four of the five previous rings while copper and zinc tightened theirs. On this ring aluminium tightened, by the largest margin on the board. The relative divergence this page flagged has closed, in aluminium's favour.

NICKEL WAS THE CLEAR LOSER ON THE BOARD AND IT LOOSENED ON EVERY LEG. Cash fell $270.00, or 1.65%, to $16,050.00 - the largest fall of any metal on the ring; the contango WIDENED to $180.00 from $155.00, comfortably the widest carry on the board; and inventory BUILT 6,048 tonnes, or 2.17%, to 284,946 tonnes, the largest build and the largest absolute visible inventory of the five. A falling price, a widening carry and a large build all agree, which makes nickel the one unambiguous loosening today and a useful reminder that the base-metals complex is not moving as a bloc.

FOUR NEW DATED COST MARKS PRINTED AND ONE OF THEM IS LOWER, WHICH IS THE MOST MOVEMENT THIS BASKET HAS HAD IN SEVERAL RUNS. From SMM weeklies dated 24-September: aluminium fluoride mainstream 11,500-12,500 yuan/tonne, edging up with the low end unchanged at 11,500 and the top of the range widening from 12,300 to 12,500; cryolite 8,300-9,000, with the low end UP 300 yuan or 3.75%; and oxygen-blown #553 silicon 9,400-9,500, up 100 yuan week on week with the rise landing in the upper half of the range. From the 23-September magnesium report, Fugu 99.90% at 15,750-15,850, a midpoint of 15,800 and DOWN 400 yuan or 2.47% from 07-September - the trend flag on that row is cut from up to down. Where a range widened at the top without moving at the bottom, the series is held flat and the fact is stated rather than smoothed.

THE SECTION 232 RATE IS RE-VERIFIED AGAINST A PUBLIC LEGAL SOURCE AND UNCHANGED AT 50% ON ALUMINIUM ARTICLES AND 25% ON DERIVATIVES, APPLIED TO FULL CUSTOMS VALUE, EFFECTIVE 06-APRIL-2026. Products made with US-smelted or US-cast aluminium carry 10%; a temporary reduction to 31-December-2027 applies 15% (or the higher MFN rate) to certain industrial and electrical grid equipment; the United Kingdom has product-specific reductions to 25% on Annex I-A and 15% on Annex I-B. A CORRECTION IS PUBLISHED: earlier runs described blanket 15% Annex I-C carve-outs for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU. The source read this run supports the equipment-category 15% band and the UK reductions but NOT a blanket carve-out for those other partners, so the narrower sourced description is what this page now carries. The arithmetic: 0.50 times cash of $3,254.00 is a $1,627.00 tariff leg, up $13.00 purely because cash rose, leaving a $776.00 market leg out of the $2,403/t US duty-paid premium - 67.7% policy.

earnings.note: STRONGEST QUARTER OF THE YEAR AT THE DOWNSTREAM END OF THE CHAIN. Fourth-quarter FY26 revenue rose 25.2% year-on-year to MYR 204.8 million (USD 50.8 million) from MYR 163.5 million (USD 40.5 million), on higher sales volumes in the group's extrusion and fabrication segment; the company reports its strongest quarterly revenue and profit of the financial year, with the headline putting quarterly profit up about 200% to roughly USD 4.5 million. The result funds a MYR 100 million (USD 24.8 million) expansion plan and a diversification away from its core solar-sector business. FIGURES ARE TAKEN FROM THE PUBLIC REPORT AS PUBLISHED; the full profit-and-loss detail below the revenue line was truncated in the public summary and nothing is inferred to fill it. A USEFUL COUNTERWEIGHT TO THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM PICTURE RATHER THAN A CONTRADICTION OF IT, AND THE DISTINCTION IS GEOGRAPHIC. SMM's 24-August daily describes Chinese downstream processing operating rates as under pressure with pre-peak-season stockpiling absent, and Chinese billet inventory is at a five-year seasonal high. A South-East Asian extruder posting 25% revenue growth and its best quarter of the year says the weakness is not uniform across Asia - which is consistent with the trade-flow story on this board, where South-East Asia is being consolidated as the major supplementary scrap source by the UAE export ban and EU tariff increase. IT IS A SMALL COMPANY AND ONE QUARTER, SO IT IS WEIGHTED ACCORDINGLY: it is evidence that extrusion demand outside China is holding, not evidence that the global peak season has arrived.

earnings.note: H1-2026 interim results: alumina sales volume 1.296 Mt (+15.0% y/y from ~1.127 Mt) but average realised selling price USD 320/t against USD 529/t (-39.5%); revenue USD 415.0m (-30.5% y/y from USD 596.8m); gross profit USD 65.5m from USD 303.9m; gross margin 15.8% from 50.9%; profit attributable USD 62.7m (-74.8%); basic EPS USD 0.10 from USD 0.46; interim dividend cut to HKD 0.16 from HKD 0.65. Cash and equivalents more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings; total assets USD 2.496bn (+11.0%). THE VALUE OF THIS DISCLOSURE IS THAT IT IS A REALISED PRICE ACROSS 1.3 MILLION TONNES, NOT AN ASSESSMENT - which makes it the single best public measurement of how far alumina has actually fallen. A 39.5% decline in realised ASP to USD 320/t, against a company-stated average international alumina price of about USD 307/t on an LME Platts basis versus about USD 447/t a year earlier, confirms from the seller's own accounts that the 2024-25 alumina squeeze has fully unwound. FOR THE METAL THIS IS MARGIN-POSITIVE AND PRICE-NEGATIVE, AND BOTH LEGS DESERVE EQUAL BILLING: non-integrated smelters buy alumina cheaper, but a lower cost curve lowers the price at which supply discipline would ever appear. THE SECOND-ORDER POINT IS THE CAPITAL: cash more than doubled to USD 666.7m with no borrowings, funding preparatory work on a 250,000 t/y Indonesian electrolytic aluminium first phase at about USD 436.6m over roughly two years with a further 500,000 t/y flagged medium term. Weak alumina prices are not slowing the ex-China metal capacity pipeline - they are being converted into it. Public disclosure only; no company-specific or confidential information is used or implied.

earnings.note: SWUNG BACK TO PROFIT ON THE PRICE CYCLE, WITH TEXTBOOK OPERATING LEVERAGE. Unaudited H1-2026 interim results, approved at an 18-August board meeting and filed 19-August: ADJUSTED EBITDA UP 64.4% TO US$1.23bn from US$748m; revenue up 10.9% to US$8.338bn from US$7.52bn; adjusted net profit US$196m against a US$194m loss a year earlier. Total sales cost rose 3.3% to US$6.31bn, attributed to higher energy costs. REVENUE UP A TENTH AGAINST EBITDA UP NEARLY TWO-THIRDS IS THE SAME OPERATING-LEVERAGE SIGNATURE EVERY OTHER PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL HAS REPORTED FOR THE FIRST HALF, and it confirms the pattern extends beyond Western and Gulf smelters. The cost line is the part worth noting rather than the profit line: sales cost rose only 3.3% while revenue rose 10.9%, so the margin expansion came from price rather than from cost deflation, and the company specifically attributed what cost inflation there was to ENERGY. That is consistent with the power and carbon risk carried on the input basket. The half captured aluminium reaching four-year highs before the retreat now visible on this board, so it is a backward-looking confirmation of the cycle rather than a forward signal.

earnings.note: Revenue RMB 11.53bn, up 32.4% year on year. Net profit attributable to owners RMB 2.30bn, up 166.1%. EPS RMB 1.11 against RMB 0.58 in the corresponding period of last year, up 91.4%. THE CLEANEST PUBLIC READ THIS WEEK ON HOW FAR SMELTER MARGIN HAS EXPANDED AT 2026 PRICES, AND IT COMES FROM AN INTEGRATED, SELF-SUPPLIED PRODUCER. The company operates 788,100 t/y of electrolytic aluminium capacity in Huolinguole, Inner Mongolia with a captive power plant, plus an alumina refining and aluminium hydroxide base in Binzhou, Shandong; it states that self-sufficiency in alumina and electricity fully meets its production requirements. Profit attributable rose 166% on revenue up 32%, which is operating leverage of roughly five times and is only possible when the price rises against a cost base that does not. Management attributes the gain to higher electrolytic aluminium selling prices, lower production cost from a rising green-energy share, and an optimised financing structure. TWO FORWARD DISCLOSURES MATTER BEYOND the quarter: 1,040 MW of wind and 110 MW of solar were commissioned by end-June with the programme roughly 66% complete and the green share expected to exceed 50%, which lowers the cost base further; and the 500,000 t/y integrated electrolytic aluminium project in Saudi Arabia, invested with partners in 2025, had completed all compliance approvals with on-site construction in full swing. That project is a dated, sourced addition to the non-Chinese capacity pipeline. THE UNCOMFORTABLE IMPLICATION FOR PRICE BULLS: margins this wide at the low end of the cost curve are exactly the condition that funds new capacity, and this disclosure shows the funding and the capacity in the same document.

earnings.note: MARGINS EXPANDED SHARPLY WITH A THIRD OF THE VOLUME GONE. Adjusted net profit Dh2.46bn, up 34% year-on-year. Adjusted EBITDA Dh4.51bn, up 11% from Dh4.07bn, with the adjusted EBITDA margin widening to 33.3% from 27.0%. Revenue FELL 10% to Dh13.54bn from Dh15.08bn as aluminium sales dropped 32% to 939,000 t and cast metal production fell 29% to 1.01 Mt following the March incident at Al Taweelah. Reported net income Dh1.74bn after a Dh725m net incident impact. The company estimates around Dh1.5bn of capital expenditure to restore Al Taweelah, most of it in 2026, and guided cast metal back to pre-incident levels in Q1-2027 with the smelter at 25% of its reduction cells as of 26-Aug-2026 (315 of 1,262). THE COMPOSITION IS A PUBLIC CONFIRMATION OF THE MARGIN STRUCTURE THIS BOARD HAS DESCRIBED ALL CYCLE. Profit rose on three named drivers - higher realised aluminium prices, stronger regional premiums and LOWER ALUMINA PRICES - while a third of the sales volume was simply unavailable. A 630 basis-point margin expansion on a 10% revenue decline is only possible when the cost side has fallen faster than the top line, and the alumina leg is the reason. IT ALSO EXPLAINS TODAY'S PRICE ACTION IN ONE LINE: the same release that showed the margin also showed the recovery date, and the market traded the recovery date. The read-across to the alumina panel is direct - if Alunorte's 50% rate ends up lifting seaborne alumina, this is the margin that compresses first across the Gulf fleet.

earnings.note: RECORD QUARTER ACROSS EVERY SEGMENT. Consolidated revenue RS 84,825cr, up 32% year-on-year; consolidated EBITDA RS 14,989cr, up 73%; net profit RS 7,013cr, up 75%. The EBITDA margin printed 16.42% against 12.31% in Q1 FY26 and 12.82% in Q4 FY26 - a 411 basis-point expansion year-on-year and 360 basis points sequentially. INDIA ALUMINIUM UPSTREAM delivered its highest-ever quarterly EBITDA at RS 7,390cr, up 81%, comfortably exceeding the prior record of RS 5,448cr set in Q4 FY26. The COPPER segment also set a record at RS 918cr, up 36%. NOVELIS, the downstream subsidiary, reported adjusted EBITDA of $516m, up 24% from $416m a year earlier and equivalent to RS 4,875cr (+37%), with net income of $164m (+71%) and adjusted EBITDA of roughly $563 per tonne, helped by the restart of the Oswego hot mill in early June 2026 and continued Bay Minette commissioning. THIS IS THE CLEANEST PUBLIC EVIDENCE AVAILABLE OF HOW AN INTEGRATED PRODUCER CONVERTS THE 2026 PRICE STRUCTURE INTO MARGIN, AND THE CONVERSION RATE IS VERY HIGH. Revenue rose 32% while EBITDA rose 73% and upstream aluminium EBITDA rose 81% - operating leverage of well over two times on the upstream leg. The mechanism is integration: captive bauxite, captive alumina and captive coal-fired power insulate the cost stack from exactly the two legs that are currently rising for non-integrated smelters, namely seaborne bauxite (SMM index $71.57/mt, +$0.70 w/w) and seaborne alumina ($356/mt FOB East Australia on the 05-Aug trade). THE CONTRAST WITH CENTURY IS THE POINT. Century Aluminum, which buys its alumina, has now cited unfavourable raw-material price realisation as its principal EBITDA headwind for two consecutive quarters; Hindalco, which makes its own, posted a record. Management had guided to roughly 5% sequential aluminium cost inflation into this quarter and still delivered a record, which says the LME move more than absorbed it. FOR THE MARKET VIEW: this is bullish for the margin narrative and neutral-to-bearish for the supply narrative, because producers earning at this level have every incentive to run flat out and to accelerate the restart pipeline.

Q1 FY27 (three months to 30-June-2026): net income $164m, up 71% year on year; ADJUSTED EBITDA $516m, UP 24% year on year; adjusted EBITDA per tonne shipped $563, up 30% year on year; net sales $5.8bn. The prior three quarters were $459m in Q4 FY26 (down 3% y/y, $544/t), $348m in Q3 FY26 (down 5% y/y, $430/t) and $422m in Q2 FY26 (down 9% y/y, $448/t) - all three depressed by the Oswego fires of September and November 2025 and by tariff headwinds. THE FOUR-QUARTER SERIES IS THE POINT AND IT IS WHY THIS COMPANY WAS CHOSEN FOR THIS RUN'S BACKFILL: it is the cleanest public evidence available of how a downstream converter recovers from an operational shock, and of what the 2026 premium environment has been worth to the downstream. Adjusted EBITDA fell for three consecutive quarters - $422m, $348m, $459m - and then stepped up 12.4% sequentially and 24% year on year to $516m in the June quarter. THE PER-TONNE LINE IS THE MORE INFORMATIVE OF THE TWO because it strips shipment volume out: $448, $430, $544, $563. WHAT IT DOES NOT PROVE IS AS IMPORTANT AS WHAT IT DOES: a converter's EBITDA per tonne rising through a period of record US premiums is consistent with the premium being captured downstream, but Novelis does not publish a split between recovered metal-price spread, recycling spread and true conversion pricing, so this page does not claim one. THE GENERIC READ-ACROSS IS THAT THE DOWNSTREAM SIDE OF THE CHAIN ENTERED THE SECOND HALF OF 2026 WITH MOMENTUM, which is consistent with Constellium and Kaiser on the same panel and with the stable $727.50 Rotterdam billet conversion spread on the premium panel.

NALCO IS THE MOST FULLY INTEGRATED PRODUCER ON THIS PANEL - IT MINES ITS OWN BAUXITE, REFINES ITS OWN ALUMINA AND SMELTS - AND THAT IS EXACTLY WHY THIS PRINT IS USEFUL RATHER THAN JUST GOOD. A company that buys none of its alumina nearly doubling profit on record volumes tells you where margin is sitting in the chain: with whoever owns the alumina. Read directly against Chalco, the largest alumina producer in the world, whose Q2-2026 attributable profit fell 26.2% year on year in a quarter when the LME cash average was above $3,200 - the difference between the two is not the metal price, which both received, but scale, cost position and product mix. IT ALSO CUTS AGAINST THE ALUMINA-COST-SHOCK RISK THIS BOARD CARRIES: an integrated refiner posting record Q1 alumina output at 5.77 lakh tonnes is evidence of alumina availability rather than scarcity, and it sits on the same side of the argument as the alumina-to-aluminium ratio near 10.7-11.3%, well below the historical norm. THE HONEST QUALIFICATION: NALCO's exposure is predominantly Indian and its cost base is domestic coal-fired, so it is a weak read on seaborne alumina tightness, which is where this board locates the risk. earnings.note: BACKFILLED INTO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A FULL FOUR-QUARTER SOURCED HISTORY. Constellium reported Q2-2026 Adjusted EBITDA of $439 MILLION, a record, taking H1-2026 to $798m, and RAISED FULL-YEAR 2026 GUIDANCE to $980m-$1.020bn of Adjusted EBITDA EXCLUDING METAL PRICE LAG with free cash flow in excess of $300m. Leverage was 1.8x at the quarter end. Management states that the 2028 targets of $900m ex-lag EBITDA and $300m of free cash flow will now be met two years early. THE METAL PRICE LAG IS THE NUMBER THAT MATTERS FOR READING THIS PAGE and it is disclosed by the company: the $439m headline INCLUDES a $129m non-cash benefit from metal price lag, so the ex-lag figure is $310m. The four-quarter ex-lag path is $196m, $213m, $262m, $310m against headline figures of $235m, $280m, $359m and $439m - the gap between the two series has widened every quarter. THE READ-THROUGH IS THE MOST IMPORTANT ONE ON THIS PANEL FOR ANYONE TRYING TO SIZE HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 EARNINGS CYCLE IS REAL. Constellium is a converter, not a smelter: it buys primary and scrap and sells rolled and extruded product, so a rising LME shows up in its results as a NON-CASH metal price lag benefit before it shows up anywhere in the operating business. That lag contributed $126m across the whole of FY2025 and $226m in the FIRST HALF of 2026 alone - it has nearly doubled in half the time. UNDERLYING PERFORMANCE IS GENUINELY GOOD, with ex-lag Adjusted EBITDA up 58% from $196m in Q3-2025 to $310m in Q2-2026 and the company pulling its 2028 targets forward by two years - but a reader who takes the $439m headline as operating performance overstates it by 29%. THE GENERAL POINT EXTENDS ACROSS THIS WHOLE PANEL: a large share of the 2026 aluminium earnings recovery is price-lag and inventory revaluation rather than volume or spread, which is exactly the kind of earnings that reverses when the LME stops rising - and the completed August board, on which aluminium's monthly mean rose 2.97% against copper's 6.12% and zinc's 7.76%, is the first evidence that it may be about to.

earnings.note: ADDED TO THIS PANEL THIS RUN WITH A PRIMARY-SOURCED HISTORY TAKEN DIRECTLY FROM SEC FILINGS RATHER THAN FROM COVERAGE. Kaiser reported record Q2-2026 adjusted EBITDA of $166.3m against $67.7m a year earlier, a 146% increase, on net sales of $1.2566bn and conversion revenue of $437.0m. GAAP net income was $96.8m or $5.72 per diluted share against $23.2m and $1.41. Adjusted EBITDA margin on conversion revenue doubled to 38.1% from 18.1%. H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA was $294.8m against $141.1m. Net debt leverage improved to 2.1x from 3.4x at 31-December-2025 and the full-year adjusted EBITDA outlook was raised to +45-55% year on year from +20-30%. Shipments rose 6% to 305.7 million lbs, led by packaging at 155.8 million lbs and aerospace/high-strength at 60.8 million. THE READ-THROUGH IS A WARNING ABOUT HOW MUCH OF THE 2026 DOWNSTREAM EARNINGS CYCLE IS A PRICE ARTEFACT RATHER THAN A DEMAND ONE, AND KAISER DISCLOSES IT MORE HONESTLY THAN MOST. Adjusted EBITDA includes management-estimated FAVOURABLE METAL PRICE LAG of approximately $27.0m in Q2-2026 and $36.0m in Q1-2026 - $64.0m across the half against $36.0m in H1-2025. That is roughly 22% of H1-2026 adjusted EBITDA arising from the timing difference between the Midwest Transaction Price embedded in cost of sales and the market price over the period, not from conversion economics. MANAGEMENT SAID SO EXPLICITLY: the raised full-year outlook 'assumes a NEUTRAL metal price lag through the end of the year, and does not assume a continuation of the metal lag or consumption cost tailwinds recorded in the first half', and the CEO said the company expects aluminium price dynamics to normalise over the balance of the year. THE COMMERCIAL LESSON FOR READING THIS WHOLE PANEL: a rising aluminium price inflates downstream converter earnings twice - once through genuine mix and volume, once through inventory timing - and the second half reverses if the price stops rising. Kaiser's underlying story is nevertheless real: conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.43 from $1.30, packaging conversion revenue per pound rose to $1.12 from $0.92, and aerospace shipments grew as destocking eased. Both things are true at once and the filing quantifies the split, which is why this row is worth its place.

A 35% profit increase at a producer with no exposure to either strongly supports the former. ITS Q2 RESULT IN LATE AUGUST IS THE MORE INTERESTING DATAPOINT, because it will cover the quarter in which alumina fell to roughly 10.7% of the metal price.

catalysts.text: THE WEEKLY CLOSE TEST AT 3,261 RESOLVED CONSTRUCTIVELY AND IS NOW CLOSED. This page published in advance that a WEEKLY close beneath 3,261 - the 38.2% retracement of the 3,855-to-3,061.5 decline - was the condition for shifting weight materially towards the bearish weekly alternate count. Friday's official sets the weekly close and three-month settled $3,267.00, SIX DOLLARS ABOVE IT. The alternate is NOT promoted and the bear scenario weight is cut five points accordingly. NOTE THE DISCIPLINE THIS PRESERVES: the daily-degree alternate raised on 24-September, when three-month closed beneath 3,261 on two consecutive daily officials, is left exactly where it was. A weekly test and a daily test are different tests and this page resolves each on its own terms.

THE NEXT LME OFFICIAL, AND IT IS THE FIRST CONFIRMATION TEST OF TODAY'S IMPROVEMENT. Two things resolve at 13:20 London. FIRST, whether the contango narrows a SECOND time after $11.50: a second narrowing would turn one ring into a sequence and would be the first genuine evidence that the five-ring loosening has ended; a widening back beyond $20.00 would make Friday the outlier. SECOND, whether visible stock finally moves after two flat sessions - the front tightened on an unchanged inventory, and a draw would supply the confirmation that Friday's board lacked. PRE-REGISTERED SO IT CAN BE CHECKED: this page will treat a second consecutive narrowing PLUS a stock draw as sufficient to upgrade the bull case again, and either one alone as insufficient.

THE NEXT CHINESE INVENTORY PRINT. SMM publishes aluminium ingot social inventory at major consumption sites on Mondays and Thursdays, so Monday 28-September is the next scheduled figure and the last before the National Day holiday. The two-week fall of 118,000 tonnes to 24-September is the steepest for that period in the 2020-2026 record; the question Monday answers is whether the final pre-holiday week extends it. A third consecutive steep draw immediately before the holiday would make the post-holiday rebuild test larger, not smaller, because pre-holiday destocking is a pull-forward by construction.

THE NEXT DATED STEP IN THE US-CANADA TARIFF SCHEDULE. The corridor is already taxed in both directions - US Section 232 at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, and Canada's counter-tariff raised from 25% to 50% on 08-September inside a package covering $27.6 billion of US imports. The relevance to aluminium is that the North American premium is the most policy-determined price on this page, at 67.7% policy on today's arithmetic, so every dated step in the schedule moves a real delivered cost rather than a sentiment gauge.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE QUARTERLY PREMIUM SETTLEMENT - STILL THE LARGEST SINGLE DATED EVENT LEFT ON THIS PAGE AND NOW INSIDE TWO WEEKS. The publicly reported pending range is $280-310/t against the settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22% to 29%, and it is carried with a null value so the chart shows a pending band rather than a false print. THE ARGUMENT MOVED AGAINST THE BUYER THIS WEEK: the exchange curve went from charging $24.50 to defer metal to charging $13.00 in a single ring, and premiums are the price of immediacy. Against that, Chinese spot metal is still clearing at discounts, ex-China capacity is recovering, and Chinese August primary imports fell 14.65% year on year. This page takes no view and will publish the figure when it is public.

CHINA'S NATIONAL DAY HOLIDAY AND THE POST-HOLIDAY REBUILD TEST - THE CLEANEST FORWARD TEST ON THE PAGE, BECAUSE IT IS THE ONE WHERE THIS PAGE HAS NAMED THE MECHANISM IN ADVANCE. The 118,000-tonne two-week destock to 24-September is attributed by its own source to pre-holiday stockpiling and a widening spot-futures spread. Both drivers reverse by design once the holiday ends: stockpiled metal is consumed rather than bought, and the spread normalises. If Chinese inventory rebuilds sharply in the first two weeks of October, the single strongest bullish number on this page will have been a calendar effect; if it does not rebuild, the destock was demand and the deficit case strengthens materially. That is a genuine binary and it resolves in mid-October.

THE NEXT WEEKLY ALUMINA, FLUORIDE AND SILICON PRINTS. SMM publishes its alumina index, national alumina operating rate, fluoride salt review and silicon industry review on Thursdays, so 01-October is the next scheduled refresh for four rows of this page that are currently carried at 24-September: the alumina index at 2,671.59 yuan/tonne, the operating rate at 76.89% on 119.62 Mt/y, aluminium fluoride at 11,500-12,500 and cryolite at 8,300-9,000. The number to watch is the alumina index: the alumina-to-metal ratio at 11.13% against a decade norm of 15-17% is what underwrites this year's producer earnings, and a rising Chinese index is the mechanism by which that normalises.

THE NEXT FEDERAL OPEN MARKET COMMITTEE MEETING, AND ITS RELEVANCE IS AT ITS HIGHEST OF THIS CYCLE. The US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.214% on the 25-September reference session, a further multi-year high, and financing cost is the most persistent bearish input on this page. WHAT MAKES THIS MEETING MORE INTERESTING THAN USUAL: on the same session that the yield made a further high, the aluminium contango NARROWED $11.50. If the curve can tighten against a rising rate, then the rate is a headwind rather than the determinant, and the October meeting will test which of those two descriptions is right.

THE MONTHLY CARBON-INPUT SETTLEMENT CYCLE. Prebaked anodes, coal tar pitch and green petroleum coke settle on monthly cycles concluding around the 17th-18th. The September cycle has printed and is carried - anodes at about 5,730 yuan/tonne, pitch at about 4,960, calcined petroleum coke at $470-525/t - and the October cycle is the next scheduled refresh for those three rows. Carbon is roughly 22-28% of smelter cash cost in aggregate across the anode, pitch and coke lines, so it is the second-largest block after power and alumina, and it is the block where this page has the least frequent data.

THE Q3-2026 PEER REPORTING SEASON OPENS AND ENDS THE CURRENT LULL. No peer result printed into this window and the freshest item on the panel remains Constellium's Q2 and H1-2026 on 29-July. Q3 is the first full quarter reported under a materially lower alumina-to-metal ratio and a materially higher long-rate environment, so it is the first clean public test of whether the 2026 margin expansion is holding. The per-company history panel carries twenty companies on exact publicly reported figures and will be extended as quarters are reported.

THE US-IRAN NEGOTIATING TRACK REMAINS PUBLIC, DATED AND UNCHANGED IN THIS WINDOW. The last dated development is 07-September reporting of Iran describing an arrangement with Oman to manage Strait of Hormuz shipping as days away, after more than three weeks of talks; nothing has been signed, and the stated US timetable still falls after the November midterms. A signed and implemented arrangement is the single largest bearish event available to this page, because it would unwind the Gulf supply premium that a substantial part of the 2026 price level rests on. Its continued absence is not evidence of progress in either direction.

risks.text: THE CONTANGO RISK IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN, AND THE CUT IS EARNED ON THE LARGEST SINGLE-SESSION SPREAD MOVE OF THIS SEQUENCE. The cash-to-three-month spread NARROWED $11.50 to a $13.00 CONTANGO on the 25-September official from $24.50, which was the widest reading of the sequence - the first narrowing in five rings, and almost half the contango removed in one ring. The eight-session sequence reads backwardations of $21.00 and $18.50, then $3.00, then contangos of $10.50, $22.00, $20.00, $24.50 and now $13.00. Because cash rose nearly twice as fast as three-month, spread and flat price moved the SAME way for the first time in five rings. This remains the single most consequential structural signal on the page because it feeds directly into every premium and term negotiation, and the Q4 Japanese settlement is inside two weeks. THE PUBLISHED REVERSAL CONDITION IS STILL UNMET: a return to backwardation beyond $15.00 on a settled official. So the arrow is down, not the risk gone.

THE FEDERAL RESERVE PATH AND THE FINANCING COST ARE HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE STRENGTHENED AGAIN. The US ten-year Treasury yield printed 5.214% on the 25-September reference session, about seven basis points above the 5.142% carried yesterday and a further multi-year high. Higher long rates raise the cost of carrying inventory, push forward curves towards contango, and raise the discount rate applied to every metals project and equity. THE QUALIFIER MATTERS MORE TODAY THAN IT EVER HAS: on the identical session the aluminium contango NARROWED $11.50, which is the cleanest evidence this page has published that the financing-cost explanation for the aluminium curve is partially right and cannot be wholly right. The arrow stays up because the rate itself keeps rising; the explanatory weight attached to it comes down.

THE CHINESE TRADE PULL IS RAISED TO UP AS A NEW NAMED RISK, AND IT IS THE MOST SUBSTANTIVE NEW FUNDAMENTAL INFORMATION IN THIS WINDOW. Customs data reported 25-September show China's August primary aluminium imports DOWN 14.65% year on year at 185,500 tonnes, with Russia supplying 178,150 tonnes or 96% of the total; net imports 163,600 tonnes, down 14.67%; January-August 1.66 million tonnes, down 3.41%. On the same day August extrusion exports printed a 2026 HIGH of 92,500 tonnes, up 9.7% year on year, with September guided lower at 85,000-92,000 tonnes on a narrowing price spread. The stated cause of the import fall is structural - capacity at the 45-million-tonne ceiling, resilient end-use demand, inventory drawn down through semis exports - but the effect on the ex-China balance is identical whatever the cause: less Chinese competition for ex-China primary units and more Chinese semis competing with Western fabricators. THIS DIRECTLY WEAKENS THE LOAD-BEARING ASSUMPTION OF THE EX-CHINA DEFICIT CASE.

TARIFF POLICY REMAINS THE DOMINANT SETTER OF REGIONAL PRICE AND THE TREND IS HELD AT FLAT - NO NEW INSTRUMENT PRINTED, AND THE RATE WAS RE-VERIFIED AGAINST A PUBLIC LEGAL SOURCE WITH A CORRECTION PUBLISHED. Section 232 is unchanged at 50% on aluminium articles and 25% on derivatives, applied to FULL CUSTOMS VALUE, effective 06-April-2026; 10% where US-smelted or US-cast aluminium is used; a temporary 15% band (or higher MFN) to 31-December-2027 for certain industrial and electrical grid equipment; UK product-specific reductions to 25% on Annex I-A and 15% on Annex I-B. Earlier runs described blanket 15% Annex I-C carve-outs for Japan, Korea, the UK, Switzerland, Taiwan and the EU; the source read this run does not support that, and the narrower sourced description replaces it. Canada's counter-tariff remains 50% from 08-September. THE ARITHMETIC: 67.7% of the $2,403/t US duty-paid premium is policy - a $1,627.00 tariff leg against a $776.00 market leg - and the tariff leg rose $13.00 today purely because cash rose.

THE STOCK DRAWDOWN IS HELD AT FLAT FOR A SECOND RUN AND THE REASON IS SIMPLY THAT NOTHING MOVED. Visible LME aluminium stock was UNCHANGED at 241,375 tonnes for a SECOND consecutive session after three consecutive draws. Two flat sessions is not a trend in either direction. WHAT IS NOTEWORTHY IS THE COMBINATION, NOT THE LEVEL: the front tightened $11.50 on an inventory that did not move at all, so whatever bid for immediacy is not visible in warehouse data. That is the single weakest leg of today's otherwise constructive board and the main reason this page will not upgrade further on one ring. What survives is the level and the week: a 1,225-tonne or 0.50% weekly draw, and a level near multi-decade lows about 9,840 tonnes below the August mean of 251,215.

THE GULF SUPPLY PICTURE REMAINS CONTESTED IN PUBLIC AND THE TREND IS MOVED FROM DOWN TO FLAT, BECAUSE A RISK DOWNGRADE SHOULD NOT BE RENEWED WITHOUT NEW EVIDENCE. Nothing operational printed into this window: Qatalum remains curtailed at roughly 60% of 648 kt nameplate on reduced gas with a second force majeure on aluminium sales outstanding and no published restart date; EGA's Al Taweelah remains at a publicly stated 18% of capacity with a return to previous output levels guided for early 2027; and Alba's restart remains corroborated at its fourth public reference with no fifth. The 07-September negotiating track on Strait of Hormuz shipping remains the last dated development and nothing has been signed. Holding at flat rather than repeating a downgrade is the honest treatment of a window in which no new disclosure landed.

THE CHINESE DOWNSTREAM OVERHANG IS HELD AT UP AND THE EVIDENCE GOT BROADER RATHER THAN DEEPER. SMM's 24-September South China review records transactions concentrated at a 250-290 yuan/tonne premium over the SHFE 2610 contract but quotes lowered repeatedly through the session, most deals concluded at actual DISCOUNTS, phased stockpiling complete, procurement slowing and spot circulation shifting to oversupply, with cashing out before the holiday the dominant driver. To that this run adds a structural leg: August extrusion exports at a 2026 high of 92,500 tonnes with September guided lower on a narrowing China-to-overseas price spread that compresses exporter margins, and processing trade gaining share over ordinary trade. A physical market clearing at discounts while exporting record volumes on thinning margins is a demand picture that depends on price, not on need.

THE COST FLOOR IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN, AND IT IS THE MOST ECONOMICALLY MEANINGFUL MACRO MOVE ON THE BOARD TODAY. European gas TTF fell 4.02% to EUR 71.93/MWh on the 25-September reference session, the largest single-session fall of this window, and Brent slipped 0.56% to $106.01 after the previous session's 3.90% jump. Power is roughly 30-40% of smelter cash cost and is the largest single line after alumina, so a falling energy complex lowers the marginal cost floor and therefore the price floor. IT ALSO WORKS THE OTHER WAY AND BOTH ARE STATED: cheaper European gas directly improves the economics of the European smelting capacity publicly guided to return, which is a supply risk rather than a price support. The arrow is down because the floor fell; the supply consequence is carried on the ex-China restart row.

THE Q4-2026 JAPANESE PREMIUM SETTLEMENT RISK IS CUT FROM UP TO DOWN, BECAUSE THE BUYER'S STRUCTURAL ARGUMENT WEAKENED SHARPLY THIS WEEK. The pending publicly reported negotiating range is $280-310/t against the settled Q3 record of $395/t, a fall of 22% to 29%, and the settlement is now inside two weeks. Premiums are the price of immediacy and the exchange curve is the cleanest public statement of what immediacy is worth: a buyer arguing for a deep cut leans on a curve that charges to defer metal, and that curve went from charging $24.50 to charging $13.00 in a single ring. THE OTHER SIDE IS UNCHANGED AND REAL: Chinese spot metal still clearing at discounts, ex-China capacity recovering, and August Chinese primary imports down 14.65% year on year. This page takes no view on where it settles and will publish the figure when it is public.

STRAIT OF HORMUZ AND REGIONAL SHIPPING DISRUPTION IS HELD AT FLAT: nothing operational printed into this window. The 07-September reporting of Iran describing an arrangement with Oman to manage Strait shipping as days away remains the last dated development, after more than three weeks of talks covering proposed inbound and outbound routes and the security and sovereignty of both states, and NOTHING HAS BEEN SIGNED. The corridor stays IMPAIRED on the evidence available. The relevance to aluminium is specific rather than general: Gulf smelters ship through it, and the firmness in ex-China seaborne alumina has been publicly attributed to Middle East transport problems lifting demand for bagged alumina and alternative origins rather than to any refining shortfall. A signed and implemented arrangement would be the single largest bearish event available to this page; its absence is not evidence of progress.

THE EX-CHINA RESTART PIPELINE IS HELD AT UP AND THE ENERGY INPUT MADE IT MORE LIKELY THIS RUN RATHER THAN LESS. Alba's operating capacity recovery remains the largest single tranche of recovered ex-China capacity in the public record this cycle, corroborated four times; Century's Mt Holly is at full capacity for the first time since 2015 on a $50m investment restarting more than 50,000 tonnes; Slovalco's first 75,000 tonnes of 175,000 is guided for Q4-2026; and Magnitude 7 Metals has guided a first potline of about 75,000 tonnes before the end of 2026. THE NEW EVIDENCE IS THE POWER PRICE: European gas fell 4.02% to EUR 71.93/MWh, the largest single-session fall of this window, which directly improves the economics of the European capacity guided to return. The limit is stated: a spot gas reference is not a smelter's contracted power cost, which is bilateral and confidential.

EU CARBON-BORDER COST IS A SLOW, STRUCTURAL RISK TO EUROPEAN DELIVERED PRICE AND IT IS HELD AT FLAT. No new dated instrument or rate change printed into this window. The 6% EU import duty plus the carbon border adjustment mechanism remains a structural floor under European delivered prices and a persistent disadvantage for high-carbon origins, which is why the European duty-unpaid premium and the Rotterdam duty-paid billet premium behave differently from the Japanese benchmark. It is carried here as a structural risk rather than a live one precisely because it moves on legislative rather than market timescales.

balance.label: Deficit - Goldman -720 kt, Norsk Hydro -900 kt, Macquarie -930 kt; Citi an outlier at -2.7 Mt. THE BALANCE VIEW IS UNCHANGED AND THE 11-SEPTEMBER DATA SHARPENS THE CENTRAL PUZZLE RATHER THAN RESOLVING IT: global primary production was reported down 1.7% year on year at 6.16 million tonnes and GCC output down 44% year on year in July to 293,000 tonnes from 523,000 - a genuine, large supply loss. YET China's August exports were 626,000 tonnes, taking January-August to 4.67 million tonnes, up 16.7% year on year, and dated commentary describes Middle Eastern and Australian ingot supply into Japan as RELATIVELY AMPLE with Asian premiums collapsing toward a $280-290 Q4 consensus. A DEFICIT IN PRIMARY UNITS CAN COEXIST WITH AMPLE REGIONAL AVAILABILITY IF THE RELIEVING METAL ARRIVES AS CHINESE SEMI-FINISHED AND ALLOY PRODUCT THAT NEVER PASSES THROUGH AN LME WAREHOUSE - which is the most coherent published explanation for why a multi-decade exchange inventory low, a widening backwardation and collapsing physical premiums are all true at once.

The published restart schedule is the reason, and it gained another dated entry on 20-August. Nanshan Aluminum's 2026 semi-annual report confirms 250,000 t/y of Indonesian aluminium and 260,000 t/y of carbon under construction at Bintan Industrial Park, with the integrated anode carbon removing one of the genuine physical constraints on commissioning new non-Chinese capacity. Alongside it: Gulf pre-incident output guided for Q1-2027 and running faster than the market expected; Slovalco 75,000 t/y from Q4-2026; Magnitude 7 Metals 75,000 t/y before year-end; Mount Holly already at full capacity and lifting US primary output by close to 10%; the Australian smelter's power secured to 2038 removing a closure risk over up to 590,000 t/y; Alunorte back at full rate; and a 500,000 t/y integrated Saudi greenfield through all compliance approvals with construction under way. These are published commitments with dates attached rather than projections, which is why the deficit is expected to narrow rather than persist at 2026 scale.

PREMIUM ASSESSMENTS ARE PERIODIC, NOT DAILY, AND NO AGENCY PUBLISHES ON A SATURDAY. Every premium row is carried at its own last public assessment date and none has been rolled forward as if new. The only figure in that panel that moves daily by design is the tariff decomposition, which is arithmetic on the official cash price rather than an assessment.

THE TARIFF DECOMPOSITION IS CALCULATED, NOT ASSESSED, AND THE TWO ARE NEVER MIXED. At a re-verified 50% Section 232 rate on full customs value, the tariff leg is 0.50 times cash of $3,254.00, or $1,627.00, leaving a $776.00 residual market leg out of the $2,403/t US duty-paid premium. Today the tariff leg rose $13.00 and the market leg fell $13.00 purely because cash rose; no physical market changed. A CORRECTION IS PUBLISHED THIS RUN ON THE SECTION 232 CARVE-OUTS. EVERYTHING ON THIS PAGE IS PUBLIC INFORMATION ONLY. No confidential, internal or company-specific commercial data appears anywhere: no realised prices, net-backs, shipping lanes, volumes, costs or internal commentary. THE ELLIOTT WAVE PANELS ARE TECHNICAL CONTEXT, NOT ADVICE, AND THE PROBABILITIES ARE JUDGEMENTS RATHER THAN MEASUREMENTS.
